rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$\frac{1}{\lambda}=RZ^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right),\quad R=1.097\times10^{7}\ \text{m}^{-1}$$
$$h\nu=\Delta E=E_{2}-E_{1},\qquad \lambda(\text{nm})=\frac{1240}{\Delta E(\text{eV})}$$
$$\text{number of lines from level } n=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ The Balmer series lies in the ultraviolet. ✅ Balmer (n₁ = 2) is visible; Lyman (n₁ = 1) is UV and Paschen onward are IR.  ·  ❌ A ground-state hydrogen atom can emit a line. ✅ Emission needs excitation first; the ground state can only absorb.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Hα = 656.3 nm (red) is the first Balmer line; Lyman limit = 91.2 nm; Balmer limit = 364.6 nm.  ·  R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹ = 109 678 cm⁻¹ for hydrogen.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Wavelength of the first Balmer line (n = 3 → 2). **Solution:** 1/λ = 1.097×10⁷(1/4 − 1/9) = 1.524×10⁶ m⁻¹ → λ = 656 nm (Hα).  ·  **Problem:** Energy of the photon for n = 4 → 2. **Solution:** ΔE = 13.6(1/4 − 1/16) = 2.55 eV; λ = 1240/2.55 ≈ 486 nm (Hβ).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: spectrum of hydrogen atom (within Atomic Structure).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning of 'spectrum'  ·  A spectrum is the ordered display of the wavelengths in a beam of radiation after dispersion by a prism or grating. An **emission** spectrum is bright lines on a dark background (excited atoms emitting); an **absorption** spectrum is dark lines on a continuous background (cool atoms removing their own characteristic wavelengths).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: The Balmer series was discovered first (1885) because it alone lies in the visible region.  ·  answer pattern for "Spectrum of hydrogen atom": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.text: • Spectrum of hydrogen atom

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Balmer (1885) found the visible series before the electron was discovered — a purely empirical formula at first.  ·  The Lyman limit 91.2 nm marks the ionisation threshold of ground-state hydrogen.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Origin of the hydrogen spectrum  ·  Each line is one electron transition: the electron falls from n₂ to n₁ and emits one photon, hν = E₂ − E₁ = 13.6(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²) eV for hydrogen. Since the levels are discrete, only discrete wavelengths appear — hence a line spectrum rather than a continuous one.  ·  ### 3. The spectral series of hydrogen

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: $$\bar{\nu}=R\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right),\qquad \bar{\nu}_{limit}=\frac{R}{n_{1}^{2}}$$  ·  $$\text{lines from level }n=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$$  ·  $$R=\frac{2\pi^{2}me^{4}}{h^{3}c}=1.097\times10^{7}\ \text{m}^{-1}=109677\ \text{cm}^{-1}$$

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: $$\bar{\nu}=RZ^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right);\qquad \lambda(\text{nm})=\frac{10^{7}}{\bar{\nu}(\text{cm}^{-1})}$$  ·  ❌ Within a series the lines get farther apart. ✅ They crowd together and converge at the series limit.  ·  ❌ Absorption lines mean the atom lost energy. ✅ The atom absorbs exactly the photons matching its level gaps, so those wavelengths are missing from the transmitted beam.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Every line requires n₂ − n₁ = 1. ✅ Any n₂ > n₁ gives a line; the number of lines from level n is n(n − 1)/2.  ·  ❌ The Balmer series starts from n = 1. ✅ Balmer lines end at n₁ = 2; the lower level defines the series, not the upper one.  ·  ❌ The number of lines from level n is n − 1. ✅ That counts one series only; the total is n(n − 1)/2.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The series limit is the strongest line. ✅ It is the *convergence* point where lines merge into the ionisation continuum.  ·  ❌ R is an empirical fitted constant with no origin. ✅ Bohr derived it from m, e, h and c — a theoretical prediction confirmed by experiment.  ·  ❌ ν̄ is the frequency. ✅ It is the wave number (1/λ); frequency ν = c·ν̄.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The same R applies unchanged to He⁺. ✅ Multiply by Z² (and apply the reduced-mass correction for precision).  ·  **Problem:** Shortest Balmer wavelength. **Solution:** the series limit, n₂ → ∞: λ = 1/(R/4) = 4/R = 364.6 nm.  ·  **Problem:** λ of the Hβ line (4 → 2). **Solution:** ν̄ = 1.097×10⁷(1/4 − 1/16) = 1.097×10⁷ × 0.1875 = 2.057×10⁶ m⁻¹ → λ = 486 nm.
